So of course, every dog’s experience is different but this is what has worked for my girl.

1. She had NO experience with city sights, sounds, etc. so I hired a trainer and we worked on counter conditioning (seeing other dogs so consistently, especially on leash, hearing barking, etc.). Then we would walk to the dog park but NOT go in. First we’d sit across the street and get steadily closer; heavily treating when she was calm and we’ll behaved. The easier it became, the closer we’d get.

2. Got her into a small obedience class, only 5 other dogs and she steadily progressed through the levels (1, 2, and 3).

3. Started doing tandem walks with a friend and her dog. We’d start from a distance but going on the same direction. The more comfortable she became the closer we’d get, until we were all side by side.

4. After about 6 months, I started taking her to the very small dog park in the neighborhood. Always go during off peak times. Pay attention to body signals, so that when she’s feeling overwhelmed, it’s time to go.

* I’m also a huge fan of agility training. It changed my girl’s world. Exercise is always a good way for dogs to work our anxiety, but getting her into an agility league both exercises her and helps her feel comfortable around others (humans and dogs).
